description:
File: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:150-213

The iterative-deepening DFS in build_path has worst-case O(pool_size^max_depth) node visits. With MAX_DEPTH=10 and a pool of N certificates, worst case is N^10 visits.

Cycle detection (lines 193-200) prunes certs whose subject DN is already in the path, which bounds the DFS by unique DNs in the pool. However:
1. An adversary can craft a pool of N certs with N distinct DNs that each topologically connect to each other, forming a complete graph. The DFS would explore all N! orderings before declaring NoPathFound.
2. Even with legitimate-looking certs (e.g., from a compromised intermediate that cross-certified many other CAs), the pool could be poisoned.

For N=20 distinct DNs and depth 10: C(20,10)*10! ≈ 670 million node visits. This is a denial-of-service risk when the cert pool is populated from untrusted input (e.g., certificates presented in a TLS handshake).

Fix: Add a visited-path-hash set (tracking the set of certs in the current path) AND a global node-visit counter with a configurable limit. When the limit is exceeded, return Error::DepthExceeded or a new Error::BudgetExceeded. Alternatively, add a max_pool_size parameter to CertPool.
notes: Exponential DFS is a real concern for adversarial inputs but pkix-path-builder is not intended for use with untrusted certificate pools in v0.1. # Security doc note added to build_path. Pool-size limits deferred to v0.2.
title: build_path: exponential DFS complexity with large certificate pool is a DoS vector
